title: Run task-sync Git exchange on macOS and Linux with the same bounded, confined process ownership as Windows (required for full sync)
outcome: Run task-sync Git exchange on macOS and Linux with the same bounded, confined process ownership as Windows (required for full sync)
acceptance: On macOS and Linux, every task-sync exchange Git command (retained-commit pinning, explicit fetch and push, target observation) runs under a confined local runner instead of refusing with UnsupportedPlatform. The runner starts Git as the leader of its own session and process group, keeps that group's id reserved (no process-group-id reuse window), and on cancellation, deadline, drop and root exit kills the group repeatedly, verifying by enumerating the group's members until only the unreaped leader remains. When it cannot prove that every in-group descendant is gone (for example a fork racing termination on macOS, or an incomplete enumeration), it returns a typed failure naming the remaining or unproven pids, never success. It bounds output and applies the same non-interactive credential-helper rules as Windows. The shipped text discloses both limits: this macOS and Linux proof limit, and that a descendant leaving the process group (by setsid or setpgid) is bounded only by the deadline for Engram's result, as Windows discloses its gap. (Narrowed with Greg's approval, 2026-11-16 about 02:23Z, relayed by Engram::Asistant, mailbox 43498a6e #1340: „Tak.” to the proposal in #1339.)

Real Git operations and process control are exercised by tests that run and pass on macOS and on Linux, including the real-Git exchange and retained-construction tests that are today compiled only on Windows, plus cancellation, deadline and drop tests. These show by member enumeration that no in-group descendant survives in the tested cases, including a child that keeps forking, and that an unproven or timed-out cleanup returns the typed failure, never success.
